Are you passionate about GxP systems and digital transformation? And would you like to take ownership of an essential part of the IT and compliance strategy in an innovative pharma company?

If yes, Pharmacosmos is looking for a GxP Cloud Engineer to join the Global IT team.

Pharmacosmos is a global pharmaceutical company with headquarters in Holbæk, Denmark and subsidiaries in the USA, United Kingdom, Germany, and China. Fueled by rapid growth and supported by over 700 employees, we continue to embrace an entrepreneurial mindset, forging global partnerships to tackle pressing health challenges and improve patient outcomes worldwide. We have a collaborative and people-centric company culture rooted in our Danish heritage and built on quality, trust, and innovation.

About the department

Our Global IT department consists of 13 dedicated professionals, with 10 based at the headquarters in Holbæk. The department is structured into four focus areas: Helpdesk, Security, Application & Operation, and Strategic Projects. This role will join the Application & Operation team and serve as the primary internal expert on GxP-governed enterprise systems.

Global IT is on an exciting journey of modernization, transitioning from a traditional support function to a strategic enabler of digitalization, compliance, and operational excellence. You will work closely with colleagues across QA, Regulatory Affairs, laboratories, and IT.

About the job

We are now strengthening our internal ownership of GxP-governed IT systems – such as LIMS, TMF, and electronic document management systems – and digitalizing the way we work across QA, regulatory, and laboratory processes.

As GxP Cloud Engineer, you will take operational and strategic responsibility for these systems, ensuring they meet validation, documentation, and compliance requirements (e.g., GAMP5, FDA 21 CFR Part 11). You will also contribute to designing and implementing new systems as part of 8–10 major digitalization initiatives planned over the coming years.

This is a highly independent and impactful role with the opportunity to shape how Pharmacosmos governs and develops critical enterprise systems in a regulated environment.

The position reports to the Senior Director, Head of Global IT.

You key responsibilities will include:

• 
Operational ownership of existing GxP IT systems.

• 
System design and architecture for new digital solutions.

• 
Driving digitalization initiatives across QA, Regulatory, and Labs.

• 
Ensuring validation, documentation, and compliance (GAMP5, Part 11).

• 
Collaborating with stakeholders and external vendors.

• 
Defining and optimizing governance and processes.

• 
Acting as subject matter expert and advisor on IT/GxP matters.

About you

To thrive in this role, you bring:

• 
3+ years of experience with GxP IT systems (5+ years preferred).

• 
Experience with systems such as LIMS, TMF, or electronic document management.

• 
Knowledge of validation frameworks (e.g., GAMP5, Part 11).

• 
Understanding of documentation, SOPs, and risk assessments.

• 
Experience with cloud solutions is a plus, but GxP expertise is essential.

• 
A proactive and structured mindset with the ability to work independently.

• 
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

• 
You thrive in a dynamic and quality-focused environment and are motivated by making a real impact across business-critical systems and processes.

Pharmacosmos offers

• 
A key role in a growing pharma company with high ambitions and strong values.

• 
An opportunity to shape how GxP systems are governed and developed.

• 
A collaborative and flexible work culture based in Holbæk.

• 
Competitive salary package incl. health insurance, lunch scheme.

• 
A global organization with an entrepreneurial and people-focused spirit.

Additional information

Your application and CV (in English) should be submitted using the link above. This recruitment is supported by Capax Recruitment. Please contact Line Kejser at lke@capax.dk or any questions about the recruitment.

About Pharmacosmos**

Pharmacosmos A/S is a global leader in carbohydrate chemistry and innovative treatments for iron deficiency and iron deficiency anaemia. Building on their foundational expertise in carbohydrate chemistry and cell cycle biology, they develop innovative treatments for unmet patient needs, with a focus on iron metabolism and blood-related disorders. Founded in 1965 and headquartered in Denmark, the team is made up of more than 700 specialists across the UK, Ireland, the Nordics, Germany, the USA, and China. Learn more about Pharmacosmos at www.pharmacosmos.com.

Ambitious and skilled Global BI Specialist to drive Business Intelligence excellence

Location: Holbæk and work from home

The company Pharmacosmos

Pharmacosmos is a family-owned, international pharmaceutical company and a global leader in the treatment of iron deficiency anaemia. Headquartered in Holbæk, Denmark, the company employs more than 650 people worldwide with subsidiaries across Europe, the US, and Asia. Pharmacosmos is experiencing continued growth and is in the midst of an ongoing digital transformation, where data and insights play a key role in supporting decision-making across the organisation.

Your role

As a Global BI Specialist, you will play a central role in strengthening Pharmacosmos’ Business Intelligence capabilities within Finance & IT – Data & Projects. Your primary responsibility will be to ensure that high-quality data and actionable insights support decision-making across the organisation.

The role is an end-to-end BI position, covering both backend data platform work and frontend reporting, combined with close collaboration with stakeholders across the business. You will work across the full BI and data stack – from Azure Data Factory pipelines and SQL-based data models to reports and dashboards consumed globally.

You will be responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimising the BI and data platform, translating complex business requirements into scalable and value-creating BI solutions. Close collaboration with internal stakeholders and external BI consultants is a key part of the role, ensuring that requirements are clarified, challenged when necessary, and implemented in a robust and future-proof manner.

You will join Data & Projects, a small and highly specialised team within Finance & IT. The team consists of a Director, a Project Manager, and two Global BI Specialists and holds overall responsibility for Pharmacosmos’ BI and data platform.

The team culture is professional, collaborative, and informal, with a strong focus on knowledge sharing, sparring, and flexibility – including the option to work from home as needed.

Who you are

You are proactive, structured, and value-driven in your approach to BI and data. You thrive in roles with open-ended challenges, where requirements evolve through dialogue rather than fixed specifications. You take ownership of your work, communicate clearly with stakeholders, and focus on delivering solutions that create real business value.

You are pragmatic and operationally minded, yet able to think strategically and contribute to continuous improvements of the BI and data platform.

Your skills and experience are within

• Advanced user of Microsoft Power BI

• Proficient in SQL, capable of working in SSMS

• Familiar with ETL pipelines/integration/workflows (e.g., Azure Data Factory, Logic Apps, Azure Functions, etc.)

• Analytical skills – you can dive into new problem areas and data domains and understand the architecture and data flows

• Motivated by improving business performance with insights from data

• Experience working with Microsoft Dynamics (Axapta, 365 BC or 365 F&O) data would be an advantage

• Advanced skills in Excel would be an advantage

Specific requirements

• Fluency in spoken and written English

• Danish resident

Personal competencies

You must be a naturally proactive person. You seek excellent solutions to large and small issues that you yourself continually identify – and you always work with a focus on delivering value.

You deal very well with open-ended ideas/problems. This means that you do not require a fixed written requirements specification – because none such can be provided. Rather, you thrive in a collaborative team where ideas are brainstormed informally, after which you drive the implementation of the project, report, or fix.

You are a self-driven and systematic individual with a keen eye for detail, always seeking ways to enhance the data platform and processes. Your robust interpersonal skills enable you to collaborate effectively with others, having natural authority while maintaining an easy-going demeanor.

With excellent analytical skills and an open-minded approach to communication, combined with your natural ability to connect with others, you adeptly tackle complex challenges.

You are known for your strong sense of accountability, consistently delivering on agreements in a timely manner. You align to agreed priorities and execute swiftly.

You are a pragmatic and operationally minded thinker, always seeking practical solutions to challenges.

Additional Information

Place of work is Pharmacosmos HQ in Holbæk. Flexible work from home opportunities can be arranged with the direct manager. Limited travel may be required (5–10 days per year). This position offers strong opportunities for professional development as Pharmacosmos continues its digital transformation and global expansion.

Contact and Application

Applications and interviews are handled on an ongoing basis. Early application is recommended.

This recruitment process is handled by Capax Recruitment. Please feel free to contact Benedikte Berg Heinild at bhe@capax.dk with questions about the position. Applications can be submitted in both Danish and English.

Company presentation

Qtechnology is a leading innovator in smart camera technology, specializing in cutting-edge solutions for industrial vision and research and development (R&D). Established in 2007 as a subsidiary of Newtec Group, Qtechnology was originally focusing on embedded vision systems for optical sorting and grading. Qtechnology is now set to launch a range of hyperspectral cameras, which, when integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning, promises transformative opportunities across diverse applications.

As the company aims to scale and establish itself as a global leader, Qtechnology seeks talented individuals to join its journey and contribute to its ambitious growth and success.

Under the leadership of CEO Lars R. Fenger, Qtechnology emphasizes building dynamic core teams and fostering a collaborative environment where innovation thrives.

Description of the department

Qtechnology are a team of highly passionate people working to change the vision industry. The team, currently contains twelve employees, and operates within a larger corporate structure under Newtec Group, providing the stability and resources of a well-established organization while maintaining the innovative spirit of a startup.

The department is characterized by a fun and informal atmosphere, underpinned by a flat organizational structure. This environment fosters creativity and encourages open dialogue, allowing team members to contribute actively to the company’s vision and success.

The team consists of highly passionate professionals with a strong technical background, who are committed to advancing the field of industrial vision technology. As part of this team, you will have the opportunity to work alongside competent colleagues, contribute to significant technological advancements, and shape the role to match both your personal and professional growth aspirations.

Introduction to the position

As the Manufacturing Manager at QTechnology you will play an integral part in establishing their test systems and define the quality assurance of their internal processes in relation to their production.

Today, all production of their cameras happens in-house. However, Qtechnology are experiencing an increase in the demand of their products. Therefore, they are now aiming to outsource their production to either Poland or Asia, which means that there needs to be created and defined internal end-of-line test systems and quality loops that can be placed at their new contract manufacturer.

In this role you will therefore have the responsibility of defining and developing these test systems, document all processes and systems while ensuring that these operate optimally. You will also play a part in coordinating the outsourcing with the contract manufacturer.

Once the production have been outsourced you will be responsible for the production planning, S&OP, and the overall internal quality assurance.

The position offers you the freedom and autonomy to define and execute your tasks, while also providing opportunities for professional development and growth.You will interact closely with a diverse and international team as well as a number of external stakeholders.

Requirements

It is imperative that you have:

• Strong experience with quality assurance, possibly from an NPI role.

• Knowledge of working with a contract manufacturer.

• Experience in describing and defining test system

• Experience with documentation of internal processes

Application and Information

For more information, please contact Mia Sonne, Capax Recruitment, via email at mso@capaxrecruitment.com.

We encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible, by clicking the “Apply now” button.

Become a key link in Pharmacosmos’ global value chain

Do you thrive in a dynamic and international Supply Chain where structure, coordination, and continuous improvement are essential? Are you motivated by playing a central role in ensuring efficient and compliant supply chain processes? If so, you might be the new Supply Chain Specialist to join their headquarters at Pharmacosmos in Holbæk. Reporting to Senior Product Supply Manager you will be part of a global Supply Chain team.

Here, you will take responsibility for day-to-day execution while also helping to build and improve processes and systems in line with their growth journey.

About Pharmacosmos and the department

Pharmacosmos is a global pharmaceutical company in significant growth, delivering more than 20 percent annual growth in recent years. Headquartered in Holbæk, they also have subsidiaries in the US, Germany, the UK, and China. More than 650 colleagues worldwide work together to develop innovative treatments within iron deficiency and related diseases.

As a Supply Chain Specialist at Pharmacosmos, you will become part of a strong and collaborative team that works closely with contract manufacturers, QA, production, customer service, and sales across both Denmark and international markets.

The Supply Chain department manages planning, sourcing, and material flows for both raw materials and finished goods, and is characterized by a dynamic and supportive culture with flat structures and broad responsibilities, giving you the chance to make a visible impact. Collaboration across functions is at the core of how they work, and you will contribute not only to daily operations but also to ongoing improvement initiatives and cross-functional projects.

The role

As Supply Chain Specialist, you will play a central role in the daily execution of supply chain activities within a GMP-regulated environment. You will act as a key link across the value chain, working closely with QA, production, customer service, sales, international contract manufacturers, and affiliates.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Taking operational responsibility for selected CMO partners in Europe and the US, including coordination, troubleshooting, and follow-up through regular meetings

• Handling order flow, purchasing, and supplier interactions while ensuring compliance with GMP standards

• Supporting affiliates with planning, reconciliations, and alignment of local needs

• Acting as a link between internal and external stakeholders to secure alignment and efficient collaboration

• Maintaining accurate and up-to-date master data in ERP, including BOMs and recipes

• Contributing to process improvements, ERP implementation, and cross-functional projects

A crucial part of the role is contributing to Pharmacosmos’ digital transformation. You will work with data-driven decision-making, support the implementation of a new ERP system, and help automate processes to create a more scalable and future-ready supply chain. With your analytical mindset and strong Excel skills, you will have the opportunity to make a visible impact.

Your profile

Pharmacosmos is looking for a candidate who enjoys hands-on supply chain work and at the same time wants to contribute to improvements and development. You bring a strong operational mindset, solid ERP understanding, and thrive in a structured yet fast-paced environment. You understand the importance of compliance and documentation and have a proactive and service-minded approach to problem-solving.

To succeed in the role, you should bring:

• Minimum three years of experience in supply chain or production planning, preferably within a GMP-regulated industry such as pharmaceuticals, life science, or food

• Solid experience with ERP systems (SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, or similar)

• Good understanding of the interfaces between production, QA, and supply chain

• Strong Excel skills and a data-driven approach

• Fluency in Danish, both written and spoken, and professional English communication skills

• Relevant education within supply chain or a related field is considered an advantage

It will be an advantage if you have experience with process optimization or system implementation.

Pharmacosmos offers

At Pharmacosmos, you will step into a central role in a growing company where you can develop both operationally and professionally. You will experience broad responsibility in a flat organization, close collaboration with skilled colleagues and international partners, and a culture built on trust, ownership, and professionalism.

Pharmacosmos offers a competitive salary and benefits package, with your daily base at their production site in Holbæk.

Application

Are you ready to take part in Pharmacosmos’ digital transformation and help further develop their infrastructure? Then send your application today.

Background

Ellab, a leading provider of innovative compliance solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotech industries, is experiencing rapid growth and is expanding its Enterprise Application capabilities to support this. They are looking for an Integration Engineer to drive the upcoming integration projects and the overall digital transformation journey that Ellab is on.

Do you find it exciting to design and develop integrated solutions to connect systems, applications, and platforms and to standardize integrations across the quote to cash and supply chain processes?

Your primary responsibility will be on designing and implementing integrated solutions between Enterprise Applications. The integrated applications will be primarily Microsoft systems. However, you will be able to influence the tooling used to integrate these. This means you will develop and maintain system integration architecture and documentation. Additionally, you should also expect to design and develop integrations to other systems and applications e.g. Datawarehouse.

Are you keen on conducting thorough testing of integrations, monitoring, and troubleshooting integration issues to ensure reliability and performance, and optimizing integration processes for efficiency and scalability?

You will be key to ensuring that the enterprise application integration architecture is always transparent, resilient, scalable, and flexible and support Ellab in becoming a data-driven organization. You will ensure data integrity and security during the application transfer process. You will make sure that Ellab’s Enterprise Applications can deliver uniform, event-based, and real-time data between applications and to the data warehouse. You will establish simple, efficient reuse of data and create and manage APIs for system interaction and data exchange.

Do you feel comfortable collaborating with different stakeholders to refine integration requirements and contribute to knowledge sharing in the team?

Daily, you will be working closely together with the Ellab technology solutions team consisting of Enterprise Applications, Data Warehousing, IT Operations, Project Management, an Enterprise Architect, and R&D. You will become a part of the Enterprise Application team consisting of 3 Application Specialists and report to the Application Lead.

You will be collaborating with teams on all levels of the organization to gather and analyze system requirements, and with vendors and third-party service providers to ensure a successful system integration. You will provide technical support and guidance for integration-related issues to IT teams and stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

• Ensuring integrations between enterprise applications, including ERP and Field Service, and soon CRM and HR systems.

• Designing, developing, and documenting integration solutions to connect Enterprise Applications and their Datawarehouse.

• Conducting thorough testing to ensure the reliability and performance of integrations between Enterprise Applications and Datawarehouse.

• Monitoring and troubleshooting integration issues.

• Optimizing existing integration processes for efficiency and scalability.

• Collaborating with stakeholders to refine integration requirements.

• Contributing to team knowledge sharing.

Skills

• Experience with integrations between Microsoft Enterprise Applications, preferably .net, message queue systems, and publish-subscribe patterns.

• Azure logic apps, Azure functions, and Azure service bus (alternatively BizTalk)

• Working with custom APIs within the Microsoft framework

• Working with integration patterns.

• Working with vendors and third-party service providers to ensure successful system integration.

• Collaborative way of working.

The Ellab team – more than just a job

At Ellab, they take pride in being more than just a workplace. They have a highly active Employee club, lots of social arrangements throughout the year, an annual skiing trip, and fitness classes in their gym room. Culturally, we encourage a positive, welcoming, and caring tone – both among the employees and from top management.

In addition, they have an informal tone and appearance, and they acknowledge that a feeling of belonging is the foundation of their employee’s success – Ellab’s success.

You will be joining a flexible team with the possibility of working from home when necessary. You will get the chance to influence your tasks and responsibilities and to develop your career in a supportive and international environment. They also offer a competitive salary and benefits package.

The hiring process

Apply today and join their mission to help the world’s leading biotech & pharmaceutical companies improve the safety and compliance needed to keep life-saving products safe.

They will review the applications as they come in, and if they are lucky to sign a contract with the right person, the job will close. Interviews will be conducted ongoing.

For any questions about the role, reach out to Line Kejser on lke@capaxrecruitment.com

About UNEEG Medical

UNEEG medical A/S is a dynamic and pioneering company in the field of medical technology. The company is committed to improving the quality of life for epilepsy patients through innovative solutions that revolutionize epilepsy treatment.

UNEEG medical’s mission is to enable continuous measurement and collection of EEG data 24/7, providing patients and healthcare professionals with deeper insights into the brain. These insights can enhance patient care by optimizing the treatment and management of epileptic seizures. UNEEG medical is at the forefront of cognitive technologies for monitoring and analyzing EEG data, with a strong presence in the European market and preparations for expansion into the USA.

With headquarters in Allerød, Denmark, UNEEG medical employs around 70 dedicated professionals across Europe. As part of this family-owned company, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute to the development and marketing of groundbreaking solutions for epilepsy patients while being part of a unique and innovative culture.

About the department

As a Biosafety and Sterilisation Specialist, you will join a small and highly skilled team of specialists in quality assurance, regulatory affairs, and clinical development. The team works closely with suppliers, external partners, and internal stakeholders, ensuring collaboration across disciplines to achieve the highest standards.

You will report to Senior Director QA, RA, and Clinical Development who provides strategic and managerial support while empowering you to utilize your expertise. To further support your role, you’ll have access to external professional advisors, enabling you to make an impact within the organization.

About the role

In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring the safety and compliance of UNEEG medical’s products through comprehensive biological evaluation and sterilization processes. Your work will span the entire product lifecycle, with a focus on biocompatibility, sterilization, and cleaning validation.

Key responsibilities include planning, executing, and documenting chemical and biological tests, preparing critical documentation such as biological evaluation reports and FDA submissions, and overseeing sterilization validation and testing. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, internal stakeholders, and external partners to deliver solutions that meet stringent global standards.

This position offers an exciting opportunity to leverage your expertise in toxicology, biology, chemistry, or health technology engineering in a dynamic and innovative work environment.

Key responsibilities

• Prepare biological evaluation reports, toxicological risk assessments, biological equivalence reports, FDA submissions, and material compatibility assessments.

• Plan, execute, and document chemical and biological tests for products.

• Develop and maintain sterilization documentation, including annual reporting.

• Plan, execute, and document sterility testing, cleaning processes, and sterilization validation.

• Collaborate with internal teams and external partners, including contract laboratories.

• Stay updated on legislation governing biological safety, chemical compliance, and sterilization for medical devices to ensure regulatory compliance.

Are you ready to join a pioneering company that is transforming epilepsy treatment and improving patient care?

Apply now to become a Biosafety and Sterilisation Specialist at UNEEG medical A/S through Capax, and contribute to developing tomorrow’s medical solutions!

Capax Recruitment is assisting UNEEG Medical in this recruitment. For further information please contact Vjollca Muaremi vmu@capax.dk.

About the company

Pharmacosmos is a family-owned, international pharmaceutical company with over 50 years of innovation and leadership in injectable iron and carbohydrate polymers. Recognized as a world leader in the treatment of iron deficiency anemia, Pharmacosmos operates an advanced production facility in Holbæk, Denmark, specializing in the manufacture of iron complexes and carbohydrate-based active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).

As a research-driven organization, Pharmacosmos is committed to improving the lives of patients with iron deficiency. With a global presence spanning more than 80 countries and subsidiaries in key markets such as the Nordic region, Germany, the United Kingdom, China, and the United States, Pharmacosmos employs over 600 professionals dedicated to making a meaningful impact on global health.

About the department

Pharmacosmos’ Global IT department consists of ten specialists, with seven based at the headquarters in Holbæk. The department is divided into four key focus areas: Helpdesk, Security, Application & Operations, and PMO. This role will be part of the Security team.

The IT department is undergoing a transformation, evolving from a traditional helpdesk-oriented function to a strategic enabler of business growth and innovation. The company’s culture is built on trust, responsibility, and a commitment to quality and innovation, fostering an environment where employees can make a meaningful impact and collaborate closely with motivated colleagues.

About the position

As a GRC Specialist, you will play a pivotal role in translating security policies into practical measures, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, and enhancing the company’s overall security posture.

The primary focus of this position is governance, risk, and compliance (GRC), as well as technical security policy implementation. While direct security monitoring and incident response are handled externally, you will work closely with the Operational Security Engineer and external security partners to develop and enforce security policies and align the company’s security framework with ISO 27001, NIST, European pharmaceutical regulations, FDA, and NIS2.

With a global scope, this role ensures the implementation of security policies across all Pharmacosmos sites and subsidiaries. You will help strengthen security measures across over 2,000 endpoints, including employee devices, servers, and manufacturing systems, with the long-term goal of achieving 80-90% compliance with ISO 27001 within the next 2-3 years.

Key responsibilities

• Translate security policies into technical security measures and oversee their implementation.

• Develop and enforce security policies aligned with ISO 27001, NIST, European pharmaceutical regulations, FDA, and NIS2 requirements.

• Collaborate with external security partners (itm8 and Dubex) to address security findings and enhance the company’s security posture.

• Work closely with internal stakeholders to ensure security requirements are effectively implemented across global sites and subsidiaries.

• Assist in conducting risk assessments and ensure accurate risk profiling.

• Present security updates and risk assessments to senior leadership.

• Contribute to the development of security control reports, working towards ISO 27001 certification.

Requirements

• 3-4 years of experience in governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) or IT security policy implementation.

• Strong understanding and interest in working with ISO 27001, NIST, and regulatory frameworks (NIS2, FDA, European pharmaceutical regulations).

• Experience in a regulated industry (e.g., pharmaceutical, finance, healthcare, or similar) is highly preferred.

• Ability to write and implement security policies.

• Familiarity with risk assessments and control reporting.

• Experience working in a global security environment is a plus.

Why join Pharmacosmos?

In this role, you have the opportunity to enhance both your personal and professional skills while contributing to Pharmacosmos’ ongoing global growth. Employee development is a key priority, with a strong emphasis on continuous training, courses, and participation in relevant conferences.

At Pharmacosmos, you will be part of a supportive organization that values balance, respect, and the well-being of its employees. You will collaborate with skilled colleagues who are eager to learn and grow together while contributing to strategic IT initiatives.

Capax Recruitment is assisting Pharmacosmos in this recruitment. For further information, please contact Freja Borre Bøbel on fhe@capaxrecruitment.com.

Do you have a strong understanding of regulatory authorities and wastewater management? Would you like to be the key link that connects planning, operations, and regulatory authorities in everyday practice?

At Novafos, we are looking for a Municipality Manager to work closely with Gentofte Municipality and ensure effective handling of stormwater, wastewater, and climate adaptation—both in daily operations and long-term planning.

You will serve as a central point of contact between the municipality and Novafos, taking on a varied role where technical insight, dialogue, and coordination are essential.

A role with professional responsibility and close cross-functional collaboration

As Municipality Manager for Gentofte Municipality, you will have a broad area of responsibility with many touchpoints—both internally within Novafos and externally with the municipality, citizens, and consultants. Internally, you will work closely with our Operations Department, project managers, and specialists, and you will be an important sparring partner to the Programme Manager responsible for coordinating Novafos’ climate adaptation projects in the municipality.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Ensuring an overview of activities and tasks within wastewater and climate adaptation in the municipality

• Coordinating and following up on daily operational and wastewater-related matters, including pipelines, citizen inquiries, and ensuring professional follow-up

• Acting as a project team member in authority-related matters, including environmental impact assessments

• Assisting with regulatory cases such as discharge permits and connection approvals

• Supporting colleagues with clarification of environmental legislation, planning conditions, ownership issues, and dialogue with the municipality

• Maintaining close dialogue with operations regarding operational incidents, pipeline ownership, and wastewater facilities

• Facilitating and participating in coordination and collaboration meetings with the municipality and internally within Novafos

• Supporting the municipality’s planning processes, such as wastewater plans and related addenda

jobs.description:
PhD position in Compilation Principles for Reversible Languages (MSCA Doctoral Network E-CoRe, DC7), University of Copenhagen
 
 The position is doctoral candidate DC7, “Compilation Principles for Reversible Languages", in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network E-CoRe. The position is available from 1 January 2027, or after agreement.
 
 Job description
 The Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section, part of the Department of Computer Science (DIKU), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a 3-year PhD position on compilation principles for reversible languages.
 
 The project
 The position is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks (MSCA-DN) programme, grant agreement no. 101120187. The project advances the science and practice of reversible computing for a sustainable digital future. Energy is a main concern in society: IT accounts for an estimated 10% of global energy consumption. Reversible computation discards no information and therefore avoids the fundamental energy lower bound of conventional computing. The network trains a cohort of doctoral candidates who will improve and popularise reversible languages, algorithms, and architectures for energy-intensive applications. 

  Read more about the network at https://e-core.nws.cs.unibo.it/.
 
 The position is open for talented candidates with a master’s degree, who want to pursue a PhD degree in Computer Science.

  DC7: The successful PhD candidate will work on compilation principles and techniques for reversible languages. The candidate can build on the work by project members. 

  Concretely, the work includes the following:

   	
• Studying techniques for translating high-level reversible languages into efficient low-level reversible and irreversible representations. 	
• Designing optimisation techniques for reversible languages, including foundational methods and novel approaches to program analysis and code generation. 	
• Implementing prototype compilers to evaluate optimisation techniques, alongside a benchmark suite specifically designed for reversible compilation and empirical evaluation. 	
• Publishing the results at international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.   Planned Secondments: Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen (Germany), University of Manchester (UK).

  Key criteria for the assessment of applicants for the position:  

  The candidate must have a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish Master's degree) in Computer Science or a closely related field, obtained by the recruitment date.

  Certified copy of original Master of Science diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

  As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database: https://ufsn.dk/english/education/recognition-and-transparency/find-assessments/assessment-database/ 

  Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science.

  Other important criteria are:

   	
• Strong academic record and motivation for doctoral research.  	
• Experience in compiler design, program analysis, and language semantics, regardless of programming paradigm, is an advantage. Prior knowledge of reversible computing is not needed. 	
• Ability to work independently, take initiative, and collaborate effectively in an international research environment. Proactive and team-oriented approach to work. 	
• Proficiency in written and spoken English. 	
• Willingness and ability to travel and undertake secondments at other project partners.   The successful candidate will be employed as a PhD student at the Department of Computer Science at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Copenhagen, and will collaborate closely with the group at the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, which is also an E-CoRe partner. The position may involve co-supervising related student projects. The PhD student is expected to participate in the activities of the research section and in the training programme of the E-CoRe network.
 The main supervisor is Professor Robert Glück (e-mail: glueck@di.ku.dk), whose current research focus is on programming languages, reversible computing, program generation, and metaprogramming.

  Start date:    1 January 2027, or after agreement with the cohort of the MSCA-DN

  Duration:      3 years

  The successful candidate will conduct independent research related to the topics above at the Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section, Department of Computer Science (DIKU). We expect the candidate to engage in an active research environment and take part in student guidance.

  Note: Another job opening for DC1 “Reversible Programming Languages” is available. More information: XXX-LINK-TO-DC1.
 
 Mobility rule
 The researcher must not have resided or carried out his/her/their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays as holidays and compulsory military service and/or Refugee Convention 1951 are disregarded.

  Eligibility as Doctoral Candidate (DC)
 The recruited DC must be doctoral candidate, i.e. not already in possession of a doctoral degree on the first day of employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible.
 
 Workplace description 
 The Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section is part of the Department of Computer Science (DIKU) at the Faculty of Science, located on the North Campus in Copenhagen. At the section we research topics such as algorithmic aspects of programming, compiler technology, functional programming, reversible and quantum computing. You will be part of an international group of PhD students, postdocs, and faculty working at the intersection of programming languages, theory of computing, and various applications.

  More information about PLTC and DIKU can be found at https://di.ku.dk/english/research/pltc/  and https://di.ku.dk/english/.

  Terms of employment 
 Salary, pension and terms of employment will be in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organization. Currently, the monthly salary starts at DKK 31,845 / approx. EUR 4,260 (August 2026-level). 
 Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.
 
 The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Further information
 For further information, please contact Professor Robert Glück (e-mail: glueck@di.ku.dk).

  International applicants may find this link useful: https://ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility) or https://www.workindenmark.dk/.

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• Master of Science diploma and transcript of records. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor will do. 	
• Publication list (if any).   Deadline for applications: Sunday 1 November 2026, 23:59 PM CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee which will consist of both internal (UCPH) and external members. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You may read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
 
 The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.description:
Are you a collaborative and ambitious master's graduate with strong intercultural awareness and a curiosity for exploring sustainability challenges across different contexts and disciplines? Would you like to help shape the next generation of sustainable and regenerative global supply chains through a unique collaboration between the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and the University of Nairobi, Kenya? DTU Management (Department of Technology, Management, and Economics) invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship at the intersection of supply chain management and organization studies. Focusing on global agricultural commodity chains, the project explores how supply chains can create positive environmental and social impacts rather than simply reducing negative ones. It examines regenerative approaches that renew ecological and social systems while being collectively organized with local communities.

The PhD position is anchored at DTU Management and contributes to the department's strategic focus on developing viable and sustainable systems. You will join an international research environment at the forefront of sustainable supply chain management and organization studies, collaborating with researchers and partners in Denmark and Kenya. The project combines literature-based and empirical research on regenerative agri-food supply chains with fieldwork and data collection in Denmark and Kenya. The project will be supervised by Associate Professor Lærke Højgaard Christiansen and Assistant Professor Lara Schilling at DTU and will include an extended research stay at the University of Nairobi under the co-supervision of Senior Lecturer Thomas Ombati and Lecturer Veronica Wambui Mwangi. 

Based in Copenhagen – consistently ranked among the world's most livable cities – you will enjoy a high quality of life, a safe and sustainable urban environment, and a thriving cultural scene. At the same time, you'll be part of a vibrant, interdisciplinary research community at one of Europe's top technical universities, known for its commitment to innovation, societal impact, and diversity.

Responsibilities and qualifications
As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how global agricultural commodity chains, such as tea or coffee, can be managed based on regenerative principles. The project offers a unique opportunity to develop an international and interdisciplinary research profile at the intersection of organization studies and supply chain management. As part of the DTU Management PhD Program, you will follow a structured research and training program that combines independent research, academic coursework, teaching, and professional development.

Mandatory requirements:

• You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.
• An educational background in the social sciences 
• A familiarity with supply chain management, organization studies, or related fields such as (human) geography
• Have a strong interest in sustainability, regenerative systems, and the organization of global supply chains
• Strong speaking and writing skills in English
Further, the following qualities will be valued highly in the assessment:

• Research vision and potential 
• Evidence of academic accomplishment (e.g., high grades, timely graduation)
• Knowledge and experience with qualitative research methods and empirical fieldwork 
• Scholarly/academic writing skills 
• Familiarity with Kenya’s socio-cultural context, or experience in settings with transferable relevance, is desirable but not required.
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms

The period of employment is 3 years. The envisaged starting date is as soon as possible. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Lara Schilling (larasc@dtu.dk) and Lærke Højgaard Christiansen (laerc@dtu.dk)

You can read more about the Department of Technology, Management and Economics at https://www.man.dtu.dk/english

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A research statement (2–3 pages) outlining your research ideas and explaining your suitability for carrying out the project. Please engage with relevant scholarly literature on regenerative supply chains and organization. The statement is intended to demonstrate your research interests and potential; it is not a binding proposal, and the research plan may be further developed and refined in collaboration with the supervisory team upon enrolment in the PhD program.
• One copy of a selected written work (e.g., master’s thesis)
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Management
DTU Management conducts excellent research at the intersection of management, technology and economics. We develop solutions in close cooperation with companies and public authorities. Our research aims at strengthening welfare, productivity and sustainability. A key element is the role of technology and its interaction with industry and individuals. The department offers a wide range of courses and programs at bachelor, master, and PhD levels across DTU's study programs. The department has 250+ employees with around half of staff coming from abroad. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

  The position concerns pharmacological studies of an important regulator of synaptic plasticity in the mammalian brain.

  Information about the research group and work place can be found at the lab (Wellendorph lab) and department (www.drug.ku.dk) websites.

  Our research
 Our lab is devoted to understanding brain mechanisms involving the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA (γ-aminobutyric acid) and its metabolite GHB (γ-hydroxybutyric acid) via their actions on their respective targets, including CaM-responsive kinase CaMKIIa. We use biochemical and pharmacological analyses in cells, tissues and whole organisms to elucidate the role of GHB and GABA targets in brain dysfunction. 

  The lab spans over many different techniques and backgrounds, making it a highly interdisciplinary work environment. In the group we value social interaction, openness and teamwork, with room for ambition and scientific excitement.

  Your job
 This specific postdoc project seeks to characterize the neuropharmacology of the target CaMKIIa using in-house generated compounds. This entails studies in vivo in mice as well as tissue- and cell-based biochemical and pharmacological analyses. We are looking for a postdoc with a strong basis in neuropharmacology particularly in vivo studies in mice and who can combine biochemistry, neuroscience and pharmacology. Your tasks will include planning and execution of in vivo experiments, primary neuron experiments and biochemical and pharmacological assays. This entails a curiosity for science and a systematic approach to doing research and exploring new ideas. In addition to doing research, it is expected that you supervise students and engage in departmental teaching according to norms (currently 100 hours of total teaching per year). 

  Profile

jobs.occupation: Assistant professor or Assistant professor Tenure Track, Department of Computer Science, Copenhagen Section
jobs.description:
Assistant professor or Assistant professor Tenure Track, Department of Computer Science, Copenhagen Section

Department of Computer Science, Aalborg University is hiring Assistant professors or Assistant professors Tenure Track starting February 1, 2027. The Assistant professor position is a 3-year fixed term full-time position, and the tenure track position, is a structured career pathway with clearly defined criteria for progression to a permanent position upon successful evaluation.

One position will be affiliated with the research group Probabilistic and Symbolic AI in the Copenhagen section.

One position will be affiliated with the research group Data Engineering, Science, and Systems in the Copenhagen section.

About the CPH Section

The CPH Section is organised around the Software education programme at AAU’s Copenhagen campus and spans a broad range of computer science research. The two positions in this call will strengthen the section’s profiles in Probabilistic and Symbolic AI (PSAI), covering probabilistic, symbolic and neuro-symbolic approaches to AI, and Data Engineering, Science, and Systems (DESS), focusing on methods and systems for managing and analysing complex data. The section also hosts research in areas including natural language processing and trustworthy AI, human-centred computing, software engineering, and distributed and interactive systems. This breadth supports collaboration across research groups and between foundational, methodological and application-oriented research.

The CPH Section is a growing and international academic environment with an informal and collegial working culture. We aim to combine high scientific ambition with openness, mutual respect and a sustainable working life. Staff have substantial academic freedom and responsibility and are encouraged to collaborate across research groups and career stages, contribute to shared research and teaching activities, and develop an independent academic profile. As a member of the section, you will be part of both a close local community in Copenhagen and broader departmental research groups and network.

Qualification requirements

Appointment as assistant professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level. The research potential of each applicant will be emphasized in the overall assessment.

Your work tasks

We offer an attractive career opportunity for promising and talented researchers from around the world. The position is a career development position with the possibility of transitioning to a tenured associate professorship. We will work together with you to develop your research talent through supervision, professional networks and pedagogical upgrading.

As tenure track assistant professor your primary tasks will be research and research-based teaching. You will teach and supervise students at bachelor’s and master’s level, and you will contribute to the development of the department through research of international quality. In your daily work, you will work closely with both Danish and international colleagues.

Your main tasks will consist of:

• Independent research of the highest international quality including publication.

• Teaching, guidance and examination of bachelor’s and master’s degree students, as well as possible supervision of PhD students.

• Some degree of contribution towards attracting external research funding.

• The opportunity to collaborate with relevant national and international research environments.

You will report to the Head of Department Peter Axel Nielsen.

Your competencies

We are looking for applicants with independent research-related qualifications at a high international level and a PhD degree in computer science or a related field, and you show potential to become one of the best in the academic field of the position. You are a clear communicator with potential of becoming a skilled group leader, and you can, under guidance, organize and conduct supervision and teaching at bachelor’s and master’s degree level. Completed pedagogical courses in supervision or similar will be a plus, as will experience with external research collaborations. We also draw attention to a stay or employment at one or more internationally recognised research institutions.

As a person, you have good interpersonal skills, are inclusive and team-oriented and able to contribute to a good work environment.

We expect you to be able to write and speak English at the academic level.

Tenure track positions are usually aimed at candidates who have not previously held an assistant professor position. In order to be assessed qualified for a tenure track assistant professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Department of Computer Science

Department of Computer Science at Aalborg University is highly regarded among researchers, students, and external partners because of our leading research, education, and collaboration. The department currently has more than 165 scientific staff, 20 administrative staff, and 1100 students.

Our research is recognized internationally and nationally to be at the highest level of excellence according to community standards, prioritizing quality over quantity. We balance applications and theory, and societal and scientific impact, applying research to solve real-world problems, while also conducing foundational research with potential long-term impact. As part of this, we are acknowledged and respected for close collaboration with industry and for applying research to create impact and value for society.

Our educations are problem-based and recognized for producing highly skilled graduates with very high employability, who are experienced with project work on solving real-world problems in diverse teams and able to think critically about the technologies they develop.

You can read more on www.cs.aau.dk, and you can read more about the TECH faculty here.

Denmark builds on a welfare system, and while taxes are high, there are plenty of welfare services including free education and healthcare including pay during paternity/maternity leave and during sickness. Find more information at the International Staff Unit – they also offer a spouse/partner programme.

Assessment in connection with transfer to associate professorship

The assessment in connection with transition to tenure as an associate professor normally takes place in the final six months of the tenure track assistant professors’ employment. However, the employee may request that an assessment take place at an earlier time in the first four years. If this assessment finds that the employee is not academically qualified, they may request another assessment within the final six months of their period of employment. A maximum of two assessments may take place.

In order to be qualified for an associate professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Appointed candidates will have to make a tenure track career plan with the head of department/immediate superior to align expectations and indicate the objectives for the tenure track’s development process. This career plan must be satisfactory followed and accomplished for the tenure track assistant professor to be assessed qualified.

Additionally, the assessment, on transition to the associate professorship, will as a minimum, emphasize the following qualifications in relation to the scientific subject area of the tenure track assistant professorship:

Research qualifications equivalent to the level that can be achieved on the basis of satisfactorily completed employment as tenure track assistant professor.

Documented scientific production at international level. Assessment will be based on up to ten selected publications selected by the employee.

Documentation of pedagogical supervision and upgrading of qualifications, including a positive written assessment of teaching qualifications. The assessment will also be based on the employee's teaching portfolio. The level of contribution to an active academic environment as well as the ability to collaborate and build relationships.

The level of experience with grant proposals and experience of communicating research to relevant stakeholders.

Appointed candidates will have to make a tenure track career plan with the head of department/immediate superior, to align expectations and indicate the objectives for the tenure track’s development process. This career plan must be satisfactory followed and accomplished in order for the tenure track assistant professor to be assessed qualified.

If the tenure track assistant professor fails to request that their qualifications be assessed in the last year of their period of employment or if they are assessed as not academically qualified, the university must immediately initiate dismissal proceedings in accordance with the collective agreement rules.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design.

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Assistant professor”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.
